provenance.note: `Identifier` takes an `IdentifierDeps` — one `fetch` method, a `pidx`, and a manager — so the reference's own class is driven against a recorder, exactly as the pinned `aiding.test.ts` does. Every recorded body is the exact string `SignifyClient.fetch` would send, with each sealed salt masked as `<SXLT>` and recorded by what it opens to. All key material derives from the pinned unit tests' own passcodes at the production Argon2 profile. `PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL`: neither passcode has ever protected anything.

notes.list: `list` is the only call in this family that sends a header: a `Range` of `aids=${start}-${end}` defaulting to 0 and 24, whose answer it reads back out of `content-range` through `parseRangeHeaders`
notes.paths: `get` and `update` encode their name with `encodeURIComponent`; the six other name-bearing paths concatenate it raw
notes.body: the request body is `JSON.stringify` of an object literal, so its field order is the literal's and an `undefined` field is dropped rather than written as null
notes.signed_request: `createSignedRequest` signs an *external* URL's request with the identifier keeper's first signer and stamps the identifier's own prefix as `Signify-Resource`, not the controller's
notes.parameters: the algorithm block a body carries is the keeper's own `params()` literal, whose key order is not the schema's: a salty keeper writes `sxlt` first and `tier` fifth where `SaltyState` declares `tier` first, and a randy keeper writes a `transferable` field `RandyKeyState` does not declare at all

group_creation.note: the member records are the group creation's inputs; their sealed salts are recorded by what they open to

randy_shape.note: random keys cannot be pinned, so this records the shape of a randy creation's request body

randy_reload_shape.note: a reloaded randy keeper takes its transferability from the identifier's own prefix, because the stored `RandyKeyState` does not declare the field its `params()` writes back

post.note: the identifier's own prefix is stamped as `Signify-Resource`, and the signature covers the *external* URL's path

get.note: with no method in the request options, the signature covers `GET` while the Request itself defaults to `GET` too

signed_request.note: the clock and the agent's key are pinned, so both signatures are exact

pinned_confirmations.note: every path the pinned `aiding.test.ts` asserts is produced here by the reference's own methods, and `clienting.test.ts` drives `createSignedRequest` itself

only_two_paths_encode_their_name.note: `get` and `update` call `encodeURIComponent`; `interact`, `rotate`, `addEndRole`, `addLocScheme`, and `members` concatenate the name raw, so an alias holding a slash addresses a different resource and changes what a signature covers
only_two_paths_encode_their_name.rust_decision: refused by construction: Roadmap 5.3's `ResourcePath` encodes every dynamic component exactly once and offers no way to skip it, so all seven paths agree with the two the reference encodes

list_range_is_inclusive_and_unbounded.note: `list` sends `aids=${start}-${end}` with no validation at all: a negative start, a fractional end, or an end below the start are all sent as written
list_range_is_inclusive_and_unbounded.rust_decision: Roadmap 5.3's `ItemRange` validates start ≤ end at construction and carries unsigned integers, so an unsatisfiable window is unrepresentable

list_without_content_range_reads_undefin.note: `parseRangeHeaders` returns `{start: 0, end: 0, total: 0}` for an absent header, so a listing with no content-range reports a total of zero while carrying entries
list_without_content_range_reads_undefin.rust_decision: the range is `Option<ContentRange>` — Roadmap 5.3 already decided an absent header is `None` rather than three zeroes — so a caller can tell an empty window from an unreported one

get_requires_key_state_by_throwing.refused: No key state for identifier group1
get_requires_key_state_by_throwing.note: `requireKeyState` throws `No key state for identifier ${name}` and is selected by a boolean parameter with three overload signatures
get_requires_key_state_by_throwing.rust_decision: two methods rather than a flag: `get` returns an `AcceptedHab` and `get_any` returns the `Hab` enum Roadmap 4.1 built, whose pending variant simply has no key state to demand

update_body_is_the_whole_info_object.note: `update` sends the `IdentifierInfo` argument as the whole body, which today is exactly `{name}`
update_body_is_the_whole_info_object.rust_decision: reproduced with a one-field `IdentifierUpdate`, so a caller cannot send a field KERIA does not read

create_body_drops_undefined_fields.expression: jsondata: any = { name: name, icp: serder.sad, sigs: sigs, proxy: proxy, smids: states != undefined ? states.map((state) => state.i) : undefined, rmids: rstates != undefined ? rstates.map((state) => state.i) : undefined, }
create_body_drops_undefined_fields.note: the body literal always names `proxy`, `smids`, and `rmids`, but `JSON.stringify` drops an `undefined` value, so a non-group creation without a proxy sends four fields and a group creation sends seven
create_body_drops_undefined_fields.rust_decision: reproduced exactly: the body is an ordered `Sad` and an absent value is not written

rotate_always_writes_member_lists.expression: jsondata: any = { rot: serder.sad, sigs: sigs, smids: states != undefined ? states.map((state) => state.i) : undefined, rmids: rstates != undefined ? rstates.map((state) => state.i) : undefined, }
rotate_always_writes_member_lists.note: `rotate` defaults `states` and `rstates` to `[]` *before* mapping them, so `smids` and `rmids` are always written — as empty arrays for a single-signature identifier — where `create` omits them
rotate_always_writes_member_lists.rust_decision: reproduced: the asymmetry is what the agent receives, and Roadmap 4.6 already exposed the two accessors with exactly these presence rules

walk.note: `create` builds its keeper at the client's current `pidx` and increments the client's copy after signing, so successive creations derive under successive prefix indices

on_failure.note: a creation that fails before its fetch leaves `pidx` untouched, so the next creation reuses the same prefix index

pidx_advances_on_the_client.note: `create` mutates `this.client.pidx` after signing, so the index is shared mutable state on the client and two concurrent creations would derive the same identifier's keys
pidx_advances_on_the_client.rust_decision: the index is an atomic counter reserved *before* the keys derive, so two concurrent creations can never collide; a creation that fails consumes its index, which the reference would have reused

event_result_re_reads_the_response.note: `EventResult.op()` calls `response.json()` on a response the caller may already have read, so a second call throws `Body has already been read`
event_result_re_reads_the_response.rust_decision: the response body is owned bytes, so `operation()` can be called as often as a caller likes and narrowing it is a decode

create_signed_request_stamps_the_identif.note: `createSignedRequest` reaches an identifier's keeper through `identifiers().get(alias)`, signs with `keeper.signers[0]`, stamps the *identifier's* prefix rather than the controller's, and mutates the caller's `RequestInit` in place
create_signed_request_stamps_the_identif.rust_decision: the Rust method takes a built `Request` and returns a new one, so the caller's value is untouched; the signing itself is Roadmap 5.5's `SigningTransport::sign_request`, which that item exposed for exactly this call

reload.note: a reloaded randy keeper takes its transferability from the identifier's own prefix, because the stored `RandyKeyState` does not declare the field its `params()` writes back

randy_parameters_write_an_undeclared_fie.reloaded_from: new RandyIdentifierManager( this.salter, undefined, undefined, undefined, new Prefixer({ qb64: aid['prefix'] }).transferable, undefined, undefined, [], undefined, aid.randy.prxs, aid.randy.nxts )
randy_parameters_write_an_undeclared_fie.note: a randy keeper's `params()` writes `nxts`, `prxs`, and a `transferable` the schema's `RandyKeyState` does not declare; on reload the value comes from the identifier's prefix rather than from the stored block, so it is derivable and never read back
randy_parameters_write_an_undeclared_fie.rust_decision: reproduced from the same source the reference reloads it from — the request's transferability when creating or rotating, the identifier's prefix when interacting — because Roadmap 4.1's `RandyState` is schema-faithful and carries no such field

non_transferable_stores_the_prefix_code_.note: `create` reuses one `dcode` variable for the prefix derivation and for the stored digest code, so a non-transferable identifier's record names the basic prefix code `B` in the field that says which digest algorithm commits to its next keys — a field governing a list that is empty either way
non_transferable_stores_the_prefix_code_.rust_decision: not reproduced: Roadmap 4.6 recorded this and stores the digest code actually used (`E`), so the request body differs in exactly that one field. A record whose `dcode` is not a digest code does not reload here.

mock_identifier_state_names_two_key_mana.note: `test/app/test-utils.ts`'s `createMockIdentifierState` writes `extern: extern ?? {}` beside the algorithm's own field, so every record it produces names two key managers
mock_identifier_state_names_two_key_mana.rust_decision: refused: Roadmap 4.1's `Hab` requires exactly one, and an `extern` block with no `extern_type` is not a key-manager state at all. The records in this fixture name one, as a KERIA response does.
